transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-11-30 14:00 PT
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Lena (Redwood SE), Tom (BluePeak CTO), Clara (Platform Lead), Rajiv (ML), Aisha (SRE)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, we'll kick off — appreciate you taking the time. Quick roll call?
[00:12] Tom: Tom here.
[00:14] Clara: Clara — hi.
[00:16] Rajiv: Rajiv.
[00:18] Aisha: Aisha.
[00:20] Ethan: Ethan, Redwood.
[00:22] Maya: Great. Agenda are: 1) go over the wildcard sensitivity sweep results, 2) perf deltas on the int8 vs fp8 runs, 3) fallback and rollout options, 4) next steps. Any additions?
[00:34] Rajiv: Would like a quick look at failure modes for multi-turn prompts — that's been noisy.
[00:39] Maya: Perfect — we'll cover that.

Summary of results
[00:45] Lena: Quick house-keeping: the signal we ran was the week-of 11/23, we ran int8 and fp8 blend variants across the 13k sample prompt set you shared. The high-level: throughput improved about 1.6x on average for int8 paths, token cost down ~35-42% depending on sequence length, but we saw localized quality regressions on about 2.3% of samples flagged by our SNR threshold.
[01:10] Clara: When you say 'localized' does that mean it was specific prompt types or random?
[01:14] Lena: Mostly prompt templates with long code blocks and html-like markup, and a handful of multi-turn clarification dialogues. There were some surprising edge-case failures — we called these 'wildcards' — where the model hallucinated a schema field.
[01:30] Rajiv: Yep, our customer flows use a lot of structured templates, so that's concerning. Can you show examples?
[01:35] Lena: I'll read two short cases — transcriptions are messy though.

Example cases (quality diffs)
[01:40] Lena: Case A: prompt includes a CSV blob and asks to infer column types. FP8 gives correct type mapping, int8 returns 'unknown' for two columns and proposes an extra 'metadata' column. That maps to a precision drop from 0.93 to 0.72 on our metric.
[01:58] Rajiv: That's a big drop. Do you see the same with int8 + KV caching enabled?
[02:03] Ethan: Good question. Short answer: the current int8 run included default KV cache behavior but we did a second pass where prefix caching was disabled and the regression attenuated slightly but did not disappear. There might be a quantization sensitivity in the attention kernels that affects long-range dependencies.
[02:20] Tom: Are we sure this is quantization and not some mismatch in tokenization or preproc?
[02:24] Lena: We sanity-checked tokenization parity. Most of these cases are algorithmic changes post-quant, not a tokenization issue.

Performance deltas
[02:34] Ethan: On the perf side, int8 avg throughput per GPU increased ~1.6x for the 512 sequence jobs, with p95 latency about +8-15ms compared to fp8 on the same hardware. For fp8 micro-batch configs we saw slightly better tail latency but lower throughput. There's a trade-off curve.
[02:58] Aisha: That p95 increase is problematic for our low-latency customer tier. What was the absolute p95?
[03:03] Ethan: Roughly 142ms p95 for fp8 and about 150ms for int8 in the mixed workloads we ran; numbers vary by batch scheduling.
[03:11] Clara: Any memory footprint differences? Our infra might prefer int8 for density.
[03:16] Lena: Memory per model shard dropped ~22% on int8. That gives you about 40% more concurrency on the same cluster in our estimations.

Discussion: trade-offs and gating
[03:30] Tom: So we get 40% more concurrency and 35% token cost reduction but small increases in tail latency and a 2-3% slice of prompts with serious regressions. How do we decide whether to accept that?
[03:45] Maya: Standard approach is staged canary + prompt-level gating: route 95% traffic to int8 but keep a 5% host for fp8 fallback for certain routes. Also automatic rollback if quality metrics degrade beyond threshold.
[03:56] Rajiv: Can we do per-prompt routing? Some of our endpoints are stricter.
[03:59] Ethan: Yes — Redwood routing supports per-route model pinning and prefix-based caches; we can add heuristics to pin templates to fp8. There's some overhead to maintain two model variants but doable.
[04:12] Aisha: What about on-prem or VPC — we want to replicate this in our staging network to ensure network differences don't change perf numbers.
[04:19] Lena: Agreed — we proposed a dedicated customer test pool topology: a small GCP private pool that mirrors your egress topology. That reduces network variance.

Wildcards and sensitivity analysis
[04:30] Rajiv: The 'wildcards' — can you define them? Are they statistically clustered?
[04:34] Lena: We saw clustering with structured templates, long code blocks, and multi-turn clarifications. Also a small cluster where the model returns incorrectly formatted JSON keys — those are brittle for you. We generated a sensitivity heatmap per token position; some positions are more fragile after quant.
[04:50] Tom: Is the heatmap something you can share?
[04:53] Maya: Yes — action item, we'll push the heatmap and per-prompt CSV to the shared drive.

Objections and security/CSP concerns
[05:02] Clara: Security question — if we keep fp8 for some routes and int8 for others, will logs be split? We need unified audit trails for compliance.
[05:10] Ethan: Logs remain centralized in Redwood Console; you can filter by model variant. There's also support for streaming audit logs to your SIEM. We support SAML SSO and KMS integration for encryption-at-rest.
[05:22] Aisha: Approved, we just need a proof of concept of the SIEM integration.
[05:26] Maya: We'll include sample CloudWatch/BigQuery sink configs.

Bench plan and dates
[05:33] Lena: Proposed bench: Redwood runs dedicated perf sweep against your test pool week of 12/7 with the customer-provided prompt set. We'll run seq lengths 128, 512, 1024 with 10 runs each and share raw logs. We recommend retaining raw token-level traces for debugging.
[05:50] Rajiv: We'll provide prompts by 12/2 and success criteria doc.
[05:54] Tom: Also, please include a defensive rollback playbook so our ops team can flip routes quickly.
[05:58] Ethan: We'll draft a one-page rollback runbook and an automated canary rule that reverts traffic when quality drops more than 1.5x of baseline.

Recap / Close
[06:08] Maya: Recap: Redwood shares per-prompt CSV & heatmap (due 12/03), Ethan runs perf sweep (due 12/06), BluePeak provides prompts + success criteria (due 12/02), Aisha opens VPC peering doc (due 12/05). Next sync: same time next week to review bench outputs unless we see blockers.
[06:25] Tom: Sounds good, thanks.
[06:27] Clara: Thanks everyone.
[06:29] Maya: Thanks — we'll circulate notes and links to artifacts after the call.
[06:33] [meeting ends]

Notes: transcript includes occasional mis-heard words: 'K-V cash' for KV cache, 'Redwood privet' for Redwood Private in auto transcription. Some speaker labels may be generic in the export.
